artifact: Categorised synthetic corpus of natural-language alarm inputs and their expected resolution. Measurement artifact only: no parser or application source was modified.
resolution: Resolution = parseLeadingTime(input, now): `local` is the targetTime wall-clock, `repeatDays` are ISO weekdays (1=Mon..7=Sun, [] = one-time), `label` is the unconsumed remainder (rest). A weekday-less interval keeps `repeatDays: []`; the server/create path derives `repeat_days` from the interval anchor (design §7). For an invalid case `local`/`repeatDays`/`label` are null and the runner asserts `parseTime` throws a `TimeParseError` whose `token` equals `rejectedToken` and whose `reason` equals `reason` ("unparseable" | "already_passed").
nowConvention: Local wall-clock ISO date-time WITHOUT a timezone offset, matching fixtures/time-parse-cases.json. Default now is Monday 21 Sep 2026 10:00 local; cases that need a Monday-is-today, forward-only, or January/December-rollover view vary it.

statusLegend.supported: Verified to pass against the current parser (machine-checked; machineVerified=true).
statusLegend.target: Should resolve this way after the grammar expansion but does not today; actual_today records current behaviour.

verification: Every `supported` case was executed against clients/core/src/time.ts via `npx tsx` (parseLeadingTime) and matched; a failing supported case would have been a corpus defect. `actual_today` on every `target` case is the live parser's real output.

grammarNotes.forwardOnly: A weekday/clock resolves to the next occurrence strictly in the future: a passed 'mon 8:30am' on a Monday is next Monday, an unpassed one is today.
grammarNotes.bareMeridiemlessHour: A bare or colon time without a meridiem is 24-hour; a meridiem implies a 1-12 hour (13pm and 0am are invalid).
grammarNotes.labelSpan: Time is the longest leading prefix; when none parses, the longest parseable span anywhere is used (trailing spans preferred), so label-first phrasing works and a stray bare integer inside a label is left alone.

semantics.dayPeriods: morning = 09:00, afternoon = 15:00, evening = 19:00, tonight = 21:00, noon = 12:00, midnight = 00:00; a passed period rolls forward (day periods, target).
semantics.intervals: intervalWeeks encodes weekly recurrence (every 2 weeks / every other <day> / every 2nd <day>); intervalDays encodes day recurrence (every <n> days). With no clock, an interval anchors to now + interval preserving wall-clock; with a weekday it anchors to that weekday's next occurrence. A weekday-less interval reports repeatDays [] and is anchored server-side (design §7).
semantics.absoluteDates: Accepted once supported: '25 dec', '25/12' (day/month), '2026-12-31', 'jan 4th', 'december 25'. No year => the next occurrence (a passed date rolls to next year).
semantics.metadata: Inline alarm metadata (target): tone words chime/digital; ramp 'Ns ramp' | no ramp=0 | quick ramp=15 | gentle ramp=30 | deep ramp=60; 'note: <text>' sets the description.
semantics.next/this-week-month: next <weekday> = that weekday in the next ISO week; this <weekday> = that weekday in the current ISO week (Monday-start, mon=1..sun=7), and a hard already_passed refusal when that instant has gone; next week = same wall-clock one week ahead; next month = same wall-clock one calendar month ahead; this weekend = the coming Saturday 00:00. `last` is not a grammar token (dropped); a weekday after it resolves forward-only and the word stays in the label.

Saturday 10:00: the current ISO week's Saturday 00:00 has passed, so `this weekend` is a hard already_passed refusal, never a past instant.
Sunday 10:00: that week's Saturday (yesterday) has passed, so `this weekend` refuses rather than silently skipping to next weekend.
A passed `this friday` inside a longer phrase no longer aborts the search: the speculative prefixes swallow already_passed and the valid trailing `tomorrow 7am` wins.
An explicit ISO year is honoured verbatim, including a past year: `2020-01-01` resolves to 2020, never rolling forward.
